lots.description:
The London Borough of Ealing is undertaking preliminary market engagement to inform the future procurement of a Universal Stop Smoking Service.

Ealing currently commissions stop smoking support through an existing universal service model. As the current contract approaches the end of its term in March 2027 the Council is reviewing and redesigning the service in response to local need, national policy developments, the emerging Ealing Tobacco Control Strategy (2026-2031) and additional investment available for tobacco control.
The future service is expected be available to people who live in the London Borough of Ealing, are registered with an Ealing GP, or work or study within the borough.

The Council is seeking feedback on a potential lead provider model, under which a single organisation would hold overall contractual responsibility for the service and provide strategic leadership, governance, quality assurance, performance management and reporting.

The Council welcomes feedback on how best to structure these arrangements to maximise reach, effectiveness, integration and value for money.

The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is to inform the future service specification, delivery model and procurement approach.

tender.title: Replacement of Corporate Telephony and Contact Centre Environment
tender.description: Link Group is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified supplier to provide, implement and support a modern, secure and resilient corporate telephony and Contact Centre as a Service (CCaaS) solution. The contract will include cloud telephony, omnichannel contact handling, intelligent routing, workforce management, call recording, quality management, reporting and analytics, PCI-compliant payment handling, integration capabilities, migration, implementation, training and ongoing support. The solution will support customer-facing and colleague-facing services across Link Group and will be delivered through a phased approach.

lots.description:
Link Group is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced supplier to provide, implement, migrate, configure and support a modern, secure, resilient and scalable corporate telephony and Contact Centre as a Service (CCaaS) solution.
The procurement will deliver a group-wide, cloud-based platform supporting customer-facing and colleague-facing services. The future solution must provide an integrated, journey-led and omnichannel contact management capability, incorporating artificial intelligence (AI), automation and advanced analytics as fundamental components of the target platform.
The scope includes corporate telephony; voice, email, webchat and digital contact channels; intelligent, intent-led and skills-based routing; IVR, queues, callbacks and voicemail; workforce management; interaction recording; quality management; PCI-compliant payment handling; operational reporting and analytics; integrations; migration; implementation; training; service management and ongoing support.
The solution must provide advanced AI and interaction analytics capabilities including speech-to-text transcription, conversational and speech analytics, automated interaction categorisation and summarisation, customer intent and topic identification, sentiment analysis and the ability to identify changes in sentiment throughout an interaction. Link Group also requires the ability to identify trends, emerging issues, repeat contact, customer effort, vulnerability indicators, service quality concerns and potential compliance issues across interactions and customer journeys.
AI capabilities should support colleagues through real-time or context-sensitive guidance, knowledge recommendations, automated summaries, suggested actions and other appropriate forms of advisor assistance. The platform must also support automated quality management and analytics across interactions, reducing reliance on small manually selected samples and enabling supervisors to identify opportunities for coaching, improvement and intervention.
The solution should support conversational AI and appropriate customer self-service while enabling effective transfer to a human adviser, with relevant customer context and interaction history retained.
AI and automated capabilities must be subject to appropriate governance, security, auditability and human oversight. Suppliers will be expected to explain how AI services operate, how customer information is processed and protected, and how accuracy, privacy, bias, transparency, data residency and regulatory requirements are addressed.
The platform must integrate with Link Group's existing and evolving technology landscape, including Microsoft 365, business applications, customer and housing systems, knowledge services, payment services and data/reporting platforms, using appropriate APIs and integration services.
Delivery will be phased, allowing Link Group to establish core telephony and CCaaS capabilities while progressively developing its omnichannel, automation, AI and analytics capabilities. The successful supplier will provide implementation, configuration, integration, migration, testing, training and transition services and ongoing operational and technical support.
Bidders must clearly identify where functionality is native to the proposed platform, provided through third parties, separately licensed or consumption-based, or dependent upon future product development or roadmap delivery.

lots.description:
Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG) and Gloucestershire Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) are seeking to commission sight testing and dispensing services for children and young people in Special Educational Setting (SES) across the ICB geographies. 
Interested providers should have the capacity and capability to provide services which are person centred with reasonable adjustments and create a supportive needs-led environment to meet the needs of individual children and young people.
The sight testing service will provide in-school sight testing and dispensing to all children and young people in residential and day SES and comprises of:
• Annual sight tests, unless a more frequent interval is clinically indicated.
• Offering corrective lenses where required. 
• Manage prompt and appropriate onward referral into appropriate established care pathways if further checks or treatment are required. 
• Providing access for any parents/carers/guardians to attend the sight test and selection of frames if they wish to do so.
• Provide an eye health outcome and vision report.
The provider must work closely with SES staff to ensure the service flexibly aligns with school capacity and schedules. The provider will be expected to engage with: 
o the SES school staff 
o parents/carers/guardians 
o children and young people attending the SES 
o Commissioners 
o the local eye health network (where they exist) 
o local optical committees 
The service is being commissioned in line with the national specification, (which can be found within Atamis). 
The contract term will be for 3 years and 5 months (inclusive of the mobilisation period) plus a possible extension of up to a period of a further 2 years. The contract is due to commence on 01 April 2027 with service delivery anticipated to commence from 01 September 2027. 
The annual contract value is £306,000 with a total maximum contract value of £1,530,000 (including extension option). 
Additional funding has been allocated for mobilisation of services, up to a maximum of £39,170.  Bidders should consider the initial purchasing of relevant and necessary equipment and other items needed to establish the service that may be covered by the mobilisation budget. 
The total funding approved is not guaranteed and will be subject to scrutiny during the mobilisation phase.

tender.title: Digital Connectivity Programme - 1gb Broadband Install and Service Delivery
tender.description:
North Lanarkshire Council (the “Council”) is undertaking a major digital transformation programme to deliver gigabit capable broadband connectivity to approximately 37,000 Council owned social housing properties across the authority area. The programme is a core component of the Council’s Digital Connectivity Masterplan and supports wider strategic ambitions including but not limited to:
-Inclusive growth,
-Tackling digital exclusion,
-Improving access to public and digital services, and
-Enabling technology enabled living within Council homes
The programme reinforces the Council’s commitment to ensuring that tenants are not disadvantaged by a lack of access to high-quality full-fibre connectivity and recognises that reliable digital connectivity is now an essential utility, underpinning access to employment, education, healthcare, welfare services and community participation.

lots.description:
The proposed Agreement is expected to be primarily focused on the design, installation and delivery of physical full-fibre connectivity, through the deployment of full fibre to the premises (FTTP) across the Council’s social housing estate.
At a high level, the scope is expected to include:
- Design and construction of a gigabit capable FTTP network serving approximately 37,000 Council homes
- Installation across a diverse housing stock, including:
x Semi detached and terraced houses
x Cottage flats
x Low rise and high rise multi dwelling units (MDUs)
- Associated civil engineering and enabling works, including:
x Cabling, ducts, chambers, cabinets and in building walls, ceilings, brickwork etc.
- Installation of Customer Premises Equipment (CPE)
- Delivery over a programme period of no more than five years from appointment
The proposed Agreement will also include a Broadband Delivery Service which will include:
- Internet router hardware to enable connectivity.
- Internet service provision to the property.
- Managed service (customer service centre to handle issues & complaints) directly to tenant.
A 14 + 5 year duration is intended for the Agreement as it should provide the Council with long-term service and cost stability, while aligning with key lifecycle events such as Year 5 benchmarking and a Year 7 technology refresh. The model also supports future broadband speed requirements and aligns with expected router replacement cycles.
Full information on the requirements of this procurement procedure are detailed within the tender documents available on the PCS-Tender platform.

tender.description:
This is a project supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB).
The CAWT PEACEPLUS Early Intervention Support Youth Hubs (EASY) project aims to establish new cross border early intervention support services for families with children and young people presenting with traits consistent with a neurodevelopmental type need or who have been recently diagnosed with a neurodevelopmental condition. 
By providing help based on presenting need/symptoms, the project aims to improve outcomes for children, young people and their families by helping families' access appropriate support, based on needs at the right time and in the right place.

Two years of Audited Accounts

Ratio Assessment Methodology
Each ratio will be scored against pre-defined thresholds and combined to provide an overall Economic and Financial Standing.
The most recent financial year will carry a weighting of 67%.
The preceding financial year will carry a weighting of 33%.
A minimum overall score of 50% based on the weighted assessment of the two financial years is required to meet the pass threshold.

Acid Test ratio - (current assets-stock)/current liabilities
Cash Interest Cover Ratio - EBITDA/Interest Payable
Operating Profit Ratio - Operating Profit/Turnover
Net Worth - Total Assets-Total Liabilities
Net Debt to EBITDA Ratio - Net Debt/EBITDA
Annual Contract Value to Turnover Ratio - Annual Contract Value/Turnover
Files Accounts Test
Audit Report Review
Please refer to the Tender Instructions document for details of the scoring of the ratio assessment.
